behaviour.sticky: pinned at top 32px (z-index 20) for the whole page scroll; overlaps the hero bottom by half its height (translateY(-50%)). In EDS the block sits in its own section, so stickiness must be page-level (e.g. sticky on main or fixed after it scrolls past), not section-level.
behaviour.desktop (>=768): centred pill, rgba(255,255,255,.85) + backdrop blur, shadow; each link = 16px red circle with a white arrow-down icon + label. Hover: bg #e0e0e0 (300ms), label #d52331, arrow plays scrollArrow .5s once.
behaviour.mobile (<768): native <select> built from the same links, placeholder option 'Jump to section:', sr-only label 'Jump to:'; on change -> target.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'}).
behaviour.click: in-page anchors with smooth scroll (html{scroll-behavior:smooth}); no scroll-spy / active state.
behaviour.anchorsRequired: Sections 3, 4, 6, 7 need ids latest, topics, service, about. The xwalk section model (models/_section.json) has only name + style; aem.js turns other section-metadata keys into data-* attributes, not ids. Needs either a section model field (e.g. `anchor`) that block or section JS turns into an id, or the jump-nav resolving targets by section name. This is a model change and needs approval (no-code-changes memory).

visualCharacteristics.purpose: Sticky in-page navigation: pill of anchor links on desktop, a native select below 768px, smooth scroll to the section whose id matches

contentPattern.notes: Placeholder 'Jump to section:' and the sr-only label 'Jump to:' are UI strings in the block code (or an optional first config row).
contentPattern.structure: one row per link: a link whose URL is the target section anchor (#latest) and whose text is the label

usage: Own section directly after the home hero.
reuseGuidance: Any long page whose sections have Anchor ids. Only in-page anchors are scrolled; other URLs navigate normally.
